title: Aftermath and Undertow
premise: Twelve years after a scandal ended her career as a piano prodigy, Yara Delacroix cleans the floors of the conservatory that once celebrated her, invisible by design. When her family's childhood house goes to auction, she learns her mother has been quietly selling everything—including the letters that could prove what really happened the night Yara's brother, Theo, drowned. To save the house and the truth inside it, Yara must confront her father, a revered conservatory director whose power still shields him, and finally say aloud what the family arranged itself around: that his ambition, not her negligence, cost Theo's life. She wins back the house but loses the family name, choosing truth over belonging—and, in the final movement, plays again for the first time.
about_author: Mara Zhou is the pen name of a former classical pianist who left performance for prose after a decade of orchestral life. She writes about institutions, inheritance, and the silences families keep, and lives near a lake she refuses to swim in.

chapters.title: The Night Shift
chapters.summary: Yara mops the conservatory's practice halls at night, listening through doors to students who play like she once did. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: the ache of proximity without participation; she has perfected invisibility, and we feel both its safety and its cost.

chapters.title: Auction Notice
chapters.summary: A legal notice arrives: the Delacroix lake house will be auctioned in six weeks. Her mother, Vivienne, insists it's time to let go. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: dread sharpening into resolve—the house holds the locked room where Theo's things remain untouched.

chapters.title: What the Water Kept
chapters.summary: Yara visits the house alone and finds her father, Edmund, already there, measuring rooms for sale. A charged, courteous standoff. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: old fear resurfacing; Edmund's charm still works on her even as she notices its cracks.

chapters.title: The Letters
chapters.summary: In the attic, Yara discovers correspondence between Edmund and the conservatory board dated the summer of the drowning—evidence he knew Theo was unsafe on the water and said nothing to protect a gala performance schedule. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: vertigo; the truth is realer than she dared hope.

chapters.title: Vivienne's Bargain
chapters.summary: Yara confronts her mother, who admits she found the letters years ago and chose silence to preserve Edmund's career—and the family's standing. POV: alternating Yara/Vivienne. Emotional beat: betrayal braided with recognition; Vivienne made the same bargain Yara has been making ever since.

chapters.title: Intermission
chapters.summary: Yara grows close to Noor, a young student whose talent reminds her of Theo, and almost tells her everything. Meanwhile Edmund offers to buy the house himself—generously—if Yara signs away its contents. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: temptation; the quiet life is offered back, priced just right.

chapters.title: Undertow
chapters.summary: Edmund discovers Yara has the letters and escalates: threatening her custodial job, hinting at her own culpability that night. POV: Edmund, then Yara. Emotional beat: rising menace; we see how power corrupts through Edmund's self-justifying interiority, and Yara wavers under the weight of complicity.

chapters.title: The Question
chapters.summary: At a family dinner staged to force reconciliation, Yara finally asks the question the whole family arranged itself around: 'Dad, why did you let Theo go out on the water?' The table shatters. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: the climax—terror, release, and the irreversible act of speaking.

chapters.title: Aftermath
chapters.summary: Consequences cascade: the board investigates, Edmund resigns under pressure, Vivienne retreats, and the auction proceeds anyway. Yara buys the house with money from selling her story—not for revenge, but to keep the room unlocked. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: grief without illusion; truth costs more than promised and gives less.

chapters.title: Coda, in D Minor
chapters.summary: Months later, Yara opens the practice hall after hours and plays Theo's unfinished piece, badly, then beautifully. Noor listens from the doorway. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: resolution—not forgiveness or restoration, but the first honest sound she has made in twelve years.
